life_summary: Gerrit Wessel Gong was born on December 23, 1953, in Redwood City, California. He grew up in California during the mid-twentieth century and pursued advanced education in international relations and East Asian studies. Before his appointment to Church leadership, Gong established himself as a scholar and academic, earning advanced degrees and conducting research on East Asian geopolitics, Sino-Japanese relations, and international diplomacy. His scholarly work focused on Taiwan Strait policy, the Korean Peninsula, and U.S.-China relations. On January 4, 1980, he married Susan Lindsay, daughter of Richard P. Lindsay, at the Salt Lake Temple, and the couple established their family while he continued his academic pursuits and Church service.
church_summary: Gong served as a missionary in Taiwan during his youth, gaining fluency in Mandarin Chinese and deep cultural understanding of East Asia. He was called to the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles in 2018, becoming the second member of Asian descent to serve in this position. He has presided over temple dedications and groundbreakings, including the Winnipeg Manitoba Temple dedication in November 2020 and the Taylorsville Utah Temple groundbreaking in October 2020. His unique background in international relations and East Asian culture has positioned him to lead the Church's expansion in Asia and foster dialogue between the Church and East Asian communities, bringing scholarly insight to theological matters.
teaching_emphasis: East Asian culture and international relations
